question: With KEY_MODE=freeze, do eval-time MT queries attend to the rewritten slots at all — and would MT-acquisition improve if the values we wrote were the teacher's own document values (i.e. perfect content)? If not, the entire value-only closed-form family is capped.
variable_under_test: AM_ORACLE_WRITE=1 (teacher's own document values copied into the selected slots) vs AM_ORACLE_WRITE=0 (closed-form solved values); everything else at the canonical EXP-007 top32 config
baseline_ref: EXP-007 top32 (QA 2.1766 / MT 2.5484), re-run in-process as the flag-off control

eval_time_mass_on_rewritten_slots_mean_o.note: probability mass on S under the FULL eval-time softmax over [512 cartridge slots || own-sequence causal prefix]. S = union over 16 documents of the per-layer selected slots (34-82 of 512 per layer).

diagnostics.raw_arrays: research_loop/state/diagnostics/ORACLE-WRITE_route_mass.json (full per-layer, all 8 cache x split combinations) and research_loop/state/diagnostics/ORACLE-WRITE.json

command: FILES CHANGED (4, all opt-in behind AM_ORACLE_WRITE, default off): (1) cartridges/am/value_solve.py +126 lines: new `oracle_teacher_value_write(keys, values, queries, selected_indices, v_doc, k_teacher=..., targets=..., assign=...)` — copies the teacher's own document value rows into the selected slots, with finite/shape assertions and the same `stats['mse']` contract as `sparse_am_value_update`; assign='mass_ranked' (default) pairs the highest-teacher-mass doc rows with the highest-student-mass selected slots, assign='sequential' is a positional copy. (2) cartridges/am/finetune.py +50: two config fields `oracle_write: bool = False`, `oracle_write_assign: Literal['mass_ranked','sequential'] = 'mass_ranked'`; an `AMUpdateStats.extra: dict` field; and a leading `if oracle_write:` branch in `apply_document_am_write_to_cache` (before the existing guarded/sparse branches) that calls the new function and records per-layer routing scalars. (3) cartridges/am/continual.py +1: carries `am_stats.extra` into the per-document record. (4) examples/qasper2/train/continual_am_sparse.py +35: env knobs AM_ORACLE_WRITE / AM_ORACLE_WRITE_ASSIGN, `_oracle_write_kwargs()` which passes the new fields CONDITIONALLY (`'oracle_write' in AttentionMatchingFinetuningConfig.model_fields`, RUNBOOK 6.10) and raises loudly if the flag is on but the imported cartridges lacks the field, plus wandb tags ['oracle','diagnostic','oracle-write-<assign>'] when on. UNIT SANITY (no GPU): oracle write on random (T=512,d=128,n=96,T_doc=900,|S|=32) — n_written=32, exactly 32 rows changed, every changed row byte-identical to a teacher doc row, none outside S, all finite, mse 0.0033 (vs solve 0.0012 on the same system), mass_on_S 0.0616, teacher_doc_mass 0.6359; edge case |S|>T_doc wrote min(|S|,T_doc)=5 rows, finite. CONFIG SANITY: driver configs built with the flag off vs on differ in exactly ONE field ('oracle_write': False->True). DUAL-CARTRIDGES SANITY: from a neutral cwd with no PYTHONPATH `import cartridges` resolves to the SIBLING repo — flag off constructs fine (stock runs safe), flag on raises the intended RuntimeError; with PYTHONPATH pinned it resolves to _explore and both construct. A concurrent DIAG-OBJ run on the other GPU (no PYTHONPATH pin) ran through this cycle unaffected, its config.yaml simply has no oracle_write field. GPU COMMANDS: research_loop/results/ORACLE-WRITE/launch_oracle_write.sh (one flock-claimed GPU, gpu1, MASTER_PORT=29501, verified CARTRIDGES_IMPORT_PATH=_explore) ran two sequential Phase-2 runs at TOP_T=32 GRANULARITY=per_layer SLOT_SELECTION=tfidf USE_IDF=0 KEY_MODE=freeze TARGET_MODE=cartridge_plus_doc RIDGE_LAMBDA=1e-4 RIDGE_SCALE=spectral DELTA_WEIGHT=1e-2 AM_EXECUTION_MODE=per_document PHASE1_CACHE_PATH=outputs/phase1_selfdistill_qwen512/cache_last.pt SYNTH_DATA_PATH=data/qasper/train/qwen_qasper_MT_task_8192.parquet MODEL_NAME=Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 NUM_TOKENS=512 EVAL_QA_PATH/EVAL_MT_PATH set, WANDB_DISABLED=0 WANDB_GROUP=B-ROUTE — RUN A AM_ORACLE_WRITE=0 (RUN_NAME=ORACLE-WRITE_control-solved-top32), RUN B AM_ORACLE_WRITE=1 AM_ORACLE_WRITE_ASSIGN=mass_ranked (RUN_NAME=ORACLE-WRITE_teacher-kv-top32). Then research_loop/results/ORACLE-WRITE/run_evals_and_diag.sh re-claimed one GPU and ran examples/qasper2/train/eval_forgetting.py on {control, oracle, phase1} x {QA, MT} (parse `Eval loss`, then kill the PID per RUNBOOK 1), followed by research_loop/results/ORACLE-WRITE/measure_route_mass.py (standalone, touches nothing in cartridges/) for the eval-time attention-mass diagnostic. DID NOT COMMIT.
observations: The flag-off control reproduced EXP-007 top32 to all 16 printed digits on BOTH splits (QA 2.1766157150268555, MT 2.5483615398406982) in a fresh process on the _explore code path, so the new flag is bit-identical when off and the sibling-import confound in EXP-007's number is ruled out; the Phase-1 floor control also reproduced exactly (QA 2.2388 / MT 3.7825). The write-ceiling oracle — the teacher's own document values copied verbatim into the tfidf-selected top-32 slots, keys frozen — gave QA 1.8955 / MT 2.3810 against the solved control's QA 2.1772 / MT 2.5524, i.e. BETTER on both axes (QA -0.282, outside the ~0.1-0.2 noise band; MT -0.171, at its edge). MT 2.381 is neither 'stuck at 2.5' nor 'down toward 1.9': perfect content in those slots closes 25% of the 0.68 MT gap to the dense@4ep bar and leaves 0.509 to go, so it does not reach the win threshold MT<=2.02 while QA (1.8955) clears its threshold by a wide margin. The routing measurement says the slots are readable but weakly: under the full eval-time softmax over [512 cartridge slots || own-sequence prefix], the rewritten slots carry 0.0927 of MT-query mass and 0.0888 of QA-query mass on the oracle cache (0.0896 / 0.0827 before the write on the Phase-1 cache) — MT/QA ratio 1.04, so MT queries do NOT preferentially route to what we wrote, and only 4/36 layers fall below 5% mass. Value-only writing with frozen keys therefore leaves ~15.5% of cartridge attention (~9% of total attention) as the entire channel, and the write itself barely perturbs routing (+3.5% MT mass, cartridge total 0.588 -> 0.596). A separate, unlooked-for signature: the SOLVED write produces values up to |984| and collapses total cartridge attention from 0.588 to 0.329 on MT (0.570 -> 0.320 on QA), with 10/36 layers below 5% mass on S, whereas the oracle's teacher values top out at |63| and leave cartridge mass at Phase-1 level. Caveats: the eval splits are tiny (QA n=6, MT n=5 batches) so the MT delta sits at the noise boundary and only the QA delta is clearly outside it; the strongest surviving objection is that the oracle changes value MAGNITUDE (984 -> 63) as well as content, so part of both gains could be a magnitude/entropy effect rather than the document content being read — a shuffled- or random-value control of matched norm would separate them and was NOT run; and the reported mass is over the union of all 16 documents' selections (34-82 slots/layer), which upper-bounds the mass attributable to any single document's 32 slots.
